reviewer: Fable 5.1 independent static review; no build, no GPU run, no source-author generation; source as pasted

analysis.scopeAndContract: Diagnostic only. fullModelQualified, gainQualified, installable, productionPerformanceClaim, busyTimeClaim forced false in withContract() and re-forced on re-encode (pure test covers tampering). No timing, no default, no main/production kernel change, no GGUF option (parseOptions refuses anything but --report), no model hash. Phase 61/62 remain closed records and the phase-62 emitter is executed only uninstrumented as the object of diagnosis. OK.
analysis.frozenCaseReproduction: frozenCase() takes min-1x64 from Q4WeightStageCorpus.synthetic() unchanged (first shape, same seed; corpus RNG consumed in the same order, so bytes are identical to the phase-60/62 runs). outDim==1 enforced. Control = Gemma4Runner.shaderSource g4_q4_matvec, candidate = actual Q4RegisterLoopEmitter.emit(descriptor), both options nil, both run uninstrumented before any instrumented kernel is compiled. reproducedMismatch is the Float bit comparison of the two 1-row outputs. Gap: reproducedMismatch is set even if an output is non-finite (the 0xFF prefill of an unwritten row is a NaN) or if uninstrumentedGuardsIntact is false; finalStatus then returns completed and attribute() proceeds. Required patch 2.
analysis.unpackLayout: Layout constants and kernel stores agree: scale at tr[b] (b<bpr), quant byte at tr[bpr + 16b + l], x bits at tr[17bpr + 32b + l] and tr[17bpr + 32b + 16 + l]; total 17bpr + inDim words; stages() slices exactly those ranges. For the register shape dbits is traced as ushort(b0 & 0xFFFF) and q after the word-select/shift, i.e. as that decoder reads them. Caveat: xBits is read from the same device buffer with the same index expression in both shapes, so that stage checks the binding, not a decoder-specific load path; it will be trivially identical.
analysis.termOrder: sumOnly stores at 32b + 2l (low nibble) and 32b + 2l + 1 (high nibble), equal to termIndex(b,l,h). The two term lines in the sumOnly copy are character-identical to the production lines (pure test asserts both in the copy and in Gemma4Runner.shaderSource). CPU runningSums iterates b, l, h=0 then h=1 and indexes x[32b + l] / x[32b + 16 + l], matching. locator() decodes index%32 into byte r/2 and nibble r%2 correctly; split indices never exceed 4*inDim-1, sumOnly never exceed inDim-1, unpack never exceed 17bpr + inDim - 1.
analysis.splitVariant: w, d*w, (d*w)*x, sum stored interleaved stride 4; stages() de-interleaves by stride. Naming the intermediates forces float rounding of d*w and p, so it is altered arithmetic by construction; the code and notes say so. Its sum stage still goes through the final gate.
analysis.cpuHypotheses: Four Swift Float models (Swift never contracts implicitly); halfToFloat is exact including subnormals, signed zero and infinities (pure test covers the edge bits used by the corpus). Models are reported as matches against the uninstrumented finals and as first-difference against the instrumented sumOnly traces, and are labelled hypotheses in the notes and in the struct names; no claim about compiled instructions. Coverage gap (limitation, not a defect): the MSL default is not safe math, so a (d*x)*w or fma(d*x, w, sum) ordering is also permitted and is not among the four models; a non-match of all four therefore does not exclude a legal compilation.
analysis.traceFinalGate: finalEqualsUninstrumented requires completion, exactly one output word and bit equality with the respective uninstrumented original; it is forced false for unpack. attributableToOriginals requires both shapes. attribute() refuses when not reproduced, when unpack differs (explicitly says the unpack kernels have no arithmetic final to tie to the originals), when unpack is incomplete, when no variant is attributable, and when an attributable variant shows no differing stage (coverage-gap branch). Gaps: (a) attributability ignores the trace run's own guardsIntact, unwrittenWords and lastTracedSumEqualsOwnFinal, which are computed and reported but never consulted; a trace whose last traced sum is not its own final, or whose trace or input guards were violated, could still be called attributable. Required patch 1. (b) The ESTABLISHED statement says the trace finals equal the originals and then speaks of the first divergence as established; equality of one final on one 64-term row is necessary, not sufficient, evidence that the traced copy ran the originals' arithmetic. The wording must present it as finals-calibrated trace evidence, not as an observed original instruction sequence. Required patch 3. (c) The notes say no fast-math flag is applied, which is true, but omit that options nil selects the compiler default (not safe math), under which contraction and reassociation are permitted in both originals and every copy; this is exactly why the gate exists and should be stated. Required patch 4.
analysis.statusAndTerminalChecks: finalStatus: notEnded only on non-terminal; aborted on error; unsupported on missing hardware, register compile error, decline or any instrumented compile error; commandBufferError on any ERROR completion; notReproduced (exit 7) when the frozen mismatch is not reproduced; completed otherwise, with the attribution verdict carried only in report fields. Status is run integrity only, as documented. Every non-terminal outcome (control, candidate, each trace) sets terminal=false and returns immediately; CLI then prints NOT_ENDED, withholds END, still writes the report and exits 5. commandBuffersCommitted taken from gpu.commandBuffers via the defer/CommitCounter pattern. OK.
analysis.cliProtocol: Order: parse, exclusive report path check (reportPathRejection with exists/parent flags), executable digest, then readyToken, then exactly GO via goAccepted(readLine) with EOF (nil) rejected before any MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice. Report written with .withoutOverwriting (exclusive), encode size checked against maxReportBytes (16 MiB) and refused without trimming. No GGUF, no model hash, no timing. Exit mapping 0/7/2/4/5/1 matches finalStatus. OK.
analysis.kernelCopyFidelity: The register-shaped copy duplicates the phase-62 emitter body line for line (fetch, funnel shift, dbits, word select, byte extraction, both term lines) with only the trace stores added. The production-shaped copy's preamble (rowBase, blk, dbits from two bytes) is asserted against Gemma4Runner.shaderSource only for the byte-read and the first term line in the pure test; the remaining lines of g4_q4_matvec were not available to this review. Any divergence there would be caught by the final gate (trace final would not equal the control), so it cannot produce a false attribution, only a NOT ESTABLISHED.
analysis.memorySafety: Trace buffer has 256-byte canaries both sides and a 0xFF payload prefill; unwrittenWords counts remaining 0xFFFFFFFF words (unambiguous for finite sums and finite x). All trace stores are gated on row==0 and bounded as computed above. Register launch is one threadgroup of 32 with row>=p.y early exit. Weight length passed to declineReason is 2g + blocks (phase 62 passed g + blocks); both satisfy the span check for this case.

requiredPatches.reason: Attributability must also require the trace run's own integrity: completed, guards intact, every trace word written, last traced sum equals its own final. These are recorded but never consulted by the gate.

reproducedMismatch must not be set from a non-finite (unwritten, NaN-prefilled) output or after a guard violation in the uninstrumented reproduction; such a run must abort (exit 1), not report completed.
requiredPatches.old: if ctlBits.count == 1, candBits.count == 1 { report.reproducedMismatch = ctlBits[0] != candBits[0] }

requiredPatches.reason: The ESTABLISHED statement must present finals-calibrated trace evidence about the traced copies, not an observed original instruction sequence. The pure test substring 'ESTABLISHED by the sumOnly trace' is preserved.
requiredPatches.old:
var s: String = "ESTABLISHED by the " + name
                s += " trace (both trace finals equal their uninstrumented originals): first divergence at stage "
requiredPatches.new:
var s: String = "ESTABLISHED by the " + name
                s += " trace, calibrated by its finals (both trace finals equal their uninstrumented originals and each "
                s += "last traced sum equals its own final; this is trace evidence about the traced copies, not an "
                s += "observation of the originals' compiled instruction sequence): first divergence at stage "

requiredPatches.reason: State that options nil is the Metal compiler default (not safe math), so contraction and reassociation are permitted in both originals and in every instrumented copy; this is the premise of the gate and of the CPU models being hypotheses only.
requiredPatches.old: "No fast-math, fma or volatile flag is applied to make either original pass; no timing is measured.",
requiredPatches.new:
"No fast-math, fma or volatile flag is applied to make either original pass; options nil selects the Metal "
            + "compiler default (not the safe math mode), under which contraction and reassociation are permitted in "
            + "both originals and in every instrumented copy; no timing is measured.",

conditionalCompilePatches.appliesIf: Metal library compile of q4fd_production_unpack or q4fd_register_unpack fails on the unused variable d (only if the toolchain treats the warning as an error; expected not to).
conditionalCompilePatches.old: if variant == .unpack { lines.append("        if (row == 0u) { tr[b] = uint(dbits); }") }
conditionalCompilePatches.new: if variant == .unpack { lines.append("        if (row == 0u) { tr[b] = uint(dbits); tr[b] += 0u * uint(d == d); }") }
conditionalCompilePatches.note: Keeps the traced scale value unchanged (adds 0). Prefer leaving the source as is if the compile succeeds; the pure emitter test is unaffected.

conditionalCompilePatches.appliesIf: Swift toolchain rejects the explicit optional rebinding in patch 1 (it should not); no change needed otherwise.
conditionalCompilePatches.old: guard let run = run else { return false }
conditionalCompilePatches.new: guard let run else { return false }

expectedTestImpact: Pure tests 18+22+29+40 unaffected: checkAttribution calls Q4FirstDivergenceVariantDiff directly and checks substrings 'NOT ESTABLISHED', 'ESTABLISHED by the sumOnly trace' and 'term 2', all preserved; checkContract status mapping unchanged; checkEmitter unchanged unless C1 is applied (still no forbidden constructs). GPU run: patch 2 can newly turn a non-finite or guard-violating reproduction into exit 1 instead of a spurious 0 or 7.
limitations: Static review only; nothing was built or run here. The reported 155.9 s build pass and the pure/EOF passes are taken from the request, not re-verified.

The full g4_q4_matvec text in Gemma4Runner.shaderSource was not available; fidelity of the production-shaped copy beyond the two asserted lines is unverified. A mismatch cannot cause a false ESTABLISHED (the final gate would fail) but could cause a NOT ESTABLISHED.

Equal finals plus equal last-sum are necessary, not sufficient, conditions for the traced copy to have executed the originals' arithmetic on this one 64-term row; the diagnostic can therefore never prove the original instruction sequence. After the patches the report says so explicitly; the JSON field name originalCauseEstablished still reads stronger than the evidence and was left for schema stability.
The xBits unpack stage reads the shared device buffer with the same index expression in both shapes and will be trivially identical; it does not probe a decoder-specific load path.
CPU hypotheses omit the (d*x)*w and fma(d*x, w, sum) orderings that default (non-safe) Metal math also permits; a failure of all four models does not exclude a legal compilation.

attribute() stops at the first attributable variant in the order sumOnly then split; if sumOnly is attributable yet shows no differing stage it returns the coverage-gap verdict without consulting split (conservative, but a split result would then go unreported in the statement).

unwrittenWords uses 0xFFFFFFFF as the sentinel, which coincides with one NaN pattern; harmless while all outputs are finite, which patch 2 enforces for the uninstrumented pair but not for individual trace words.
The register decline check passes weightLength as 2g + blocks whereas phase 62 passed g + blocks; both accept this case, but the two runs do not use byte-identical decline inputs.
